title: Heuristic reconciliation for interleaved early-termination and retransmit fragments
creator: Aria Patel
description: Background: We observe sporadic miscounts in streaming sessions when clients send early-termination frames, retransmit opaque chunks, or interleave retries on lossy networks. These cases produce either double-charges (duplicate fragments accepted as new) or undercounts (finalization missing previously buffered fragments). Goal: Add a conservative, server-side reconciliation layer that detects opaque-blob duplicates, attributes provisional credits during the session, and deterministically finalizes token accounting at session close without requiring protocol changes from clients.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate opaque fragments (identical payload hash & contiguous sequence window) are marked and not double-credited during finalization.
Out-of-order fragments that are merged at finalize produce identical total token counts to an equivalent in-order stream in >= 99.9% of synthetic test runs.
No user-visible latency regressions > 2ms p95 for hot path when reconciliation heuristics enabled.
Comprehensive unit and e2e tests covering: retransmit duplicates, truncated last-frame, compressed attachments, and mid-stream model handoff.
Monitoring dashboards show reconciliation event rate, suspect-counts, and post-reconcile deltas; alerts on >0.1% mismatch rate compared to baseline.
Rollout gated behind runtime-1.22 feature flag with gradual ramp to 100% in Dedicated and Hosted lanes before Private on-prem upgrades.
Documentation (runbook + postmortem template) added to Confluence link in attachments.

notes: Tradeoffs: Strong dedupe reduces double-charges but risks under-crediting if client legitimately resends mutated fragments; mitigated by fuzzy token-bucket compare and final tokenization pass.
We avoid changing client protocol to minimize rollout friction; this means heuristics must be conservative and auditable.
Future work: consider optional client-side monotonic fragment IDs to make reconciliation deterministic across networks (RFC for 1.23).
